title: Hosted API Launch: Endpoint Scenarios, Compatibility Matrix, Acceptance & Rollout Checklist
creator: Asha Raman
summary: Consolidated launch readiness ticket that defines product acceptance criteria, compatibility scenarios across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints, and an operational checklist to validate the hosted API surface before gated rollout.
background: We are shipping a unified hosted inference surface for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank that standardizes request/response contracts, rollout policies and observability. Prior PRDs covered feature-level behavior; this document captures cross-endpoint scenarios, backward compatibility constraints, acceptance tests, and the practical checklist for a safe regional rollout.
goals: Define non-negotiable acceptance criteria for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank before enabling default traffic
Document compatibility guarantees for existing customers and SDKs (v1 -> v2 transition paths)
Provide a deterministic test matrix to validate performance and quality regressions across model families and token lengths
Deliver a rollout checklist tying monitoring, fallback policies, and rollback controls to the launch gate
out_of_scope: Dedicated and Private deployment packaging (handled by separate PM tickets)
Model training/architecture changes (only inference-time behavior covered)
Large-scale migration automation for enterprise customers (manual migration playbooks only)
detailed_requirements: API surface: single endpoint family /v2/hosted/{service} where service is chat|completions|embeddings|rerank
Contract stability: response fields marked stable must remain present and typed the same for GA; any optional fields must be behind feature flags
Schema versioning: include 'api_version' and 'model_variant' in all responses for tracing and fallback routing
Auth & quotas: existing API keys must continue to work; rate limiting headers (X-RateLimit-*) must be emitted for all successful responses
Streaming: chat/completions must support chunked streaming with identical message framing to legacy streaming protocol
Structured output: structured result envelopes (choices[], embeddings[], scores[]) must validate against JSON schema in the docs repository
Error surface: define canonical error codes for model-unavailable, quota-exceeded, invalid-input, and internal-failure
Fallbacks: automatic fallback to compatible smaller model variant when primary model fails with SLA breach - policy configurable per customer
api_contract_changes: Renamed field 'text' -> 'content' in chat choice objects to unify streaming and non-streaming responses (compatibility shim provided for one release cycle)
Embedding vector length will be explicit in 'dimensions' meta field; clients must not infer length from array size
Rerank responses include 'score_normalized' in addition to raw 'score' to support downstream comparators
Completions will include 'token_metadata' only when requested via prompt_flags to avoid payload bloat
acceptance_criteria: API contract conformance: 100% of schema-required fields pass automated contract tests against the spec for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Backward compatibility: Legacy SDK v1 smoke tests (public SDK test suite) pass with no more than 1 non-critical warning per suite run
SLOs: 99th percentile latency under target for each endpoint: chat P99 < 450ms (short prompts), completions P99 < 700ms, embeddings P99 < 250ms, rerank P99 < 500ms in default region
Error budget validation: production canary must consume no more than 10% of daily error budget during staged rollout
Quality parity: paraphrase-based quality checks and embeddings cosine similarity baselines must show no more than 2% degradation vs baseline models for benchmark prompt sets
Observability: per-route dashboards and traces wired; sampling and traces validated end-to-end for at least one generated request -> infra trace -> model trace
Security: KMS integrations for model artifacts and per-tenant encryption flags verified in VPC mirror environment
Docs & SDKs: published API docs and SDK releases (python-js-go) with migration notes available before GA
launch_checklist: Pre-launch signoffs: PM, Eng (runtime), Security, Legal, and Support have signed the launch readiness doc
Canary plan: create canary with 1% traffic in us-west-2 for 48 hours, health checks every 1 minute
Test runs: run full test matrix (see test_matrix) against canary and record results in the launch ticket
Monitoring: ensure alert policies for latency, error rate, model-fallback frequency, and quota exhaustion are configured with runbook links
Rate limit headers: test and validate X-RateLimit-* headers across SDKs and curl clients
Streaming verification: end-to-end streaming test scripts executed for chat and completions; validate chunk ordering and resume behavior
Fallback validation: induce model OOM on a canary node and confirm automatic fallback triggers without returning 5xx to customer
Docs publish: API docs, migration notice, and changelog entries deployed to docs.redwood.ai
SDK releases: cut python/js/go SDKs and verify integration tests against staging endpoint
Stakeholder comms: send pre-launch email with rollback plan and escalation matrix to sales, success, and beta customers
Rollback plan: feature flag-enabled disable for default routing, manual cutover instructions and expected downtime estimate documented
GA gating: Product + Eng + Reliability must approve after canary results; record approval in ticket
test_matrix: Smoke: single-turn short prompt across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank using small, medium, and large model variants
Latency profiles: measure p50/p95/p99 for 1-token, 128-token, 1024-token workloads across regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1)
Streaming stress: 100 concurrent streaming clients for chat with interleaved cancel/resume operations
Embeddings stability: 1000 queries batch and streaming compare vector stability across quantized vs fp16 runtimes
Rerank permutations: feed lists of 5/25/100 items to rerank and validate score distribution and ordering stability
Failure injection: simulated model crash, kernel OOM, and network partitions during active requests and validate fallback and retries
Contract fuzzing: schema fuzz tests to ensure robust error signaling for unexpected payloads
SDK compatibility: run public SDK compatibility matrix (python-js-go) and record any breakages
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Canary: 1% traffic, single region (us-west-2), 48 hours monitoring window
Stage 2 - Regional Ramp: 10% traffic to us-west-2 + 2% to eu-west-1 for 72 hours; validate cross-region fallbacks
Stage 3 - Global Beta: 50% traffic across primary regions for 7 days; invite select enterprise customers to opt-in with support on standby
Stage 4 - GA: enable default routing and remove opt-in gate after final signoff; monitor for 14 days closely with daily syncs
Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 0.5% for 4 hours, SLO breach at P99 for more than 2 hours, critical security finding
Communication cadences: daily canary report to stakeholders during ramp; immediate incident channel on trigger
Migration window: enterprise customers with custom model pins will be migrated manually with 30-day notice
monitoring_and_slo: Per-route SLOs: define SLI collection for latency, availability (5xx and model-unavailable), and quality regressions (benchmark distance)
Dashboards: token-cost by request type, per-model latency heatmap, fallback frequency; retention 30 days for operational metrics
Alerts: pager for P1 on availability, slack for P2 on performance regressions, email for P3 for cost anomalies
Runbooks: link runtime-oom, model-fallback, and high-latency runbooks to alert definitions
Synthetic tests: hourly synthetic generation across endpoints from three regions to detect regressions
migration_and_deprecation_plan: Compatibility shim: keep 'text' alias for 'content' field for two releases; warn in logs and deprecation header
Enterprise migration: manual migration checklist for tenants with pinned model versions, scheduled in weeks
Deprecation window: announced 90 days before removing shims; deprecation header inserted into responses
Data residency: migration playbook for customers in EU/APAC with guidance on region pinning
blockers_and_risks: Incomplete contract tests: gaps in schema tests could allow subtle client breakages
Latency regressions for long-sequence completions under batching heuristics
Streaming order and resume edge cases causing partial outputs to be observed by clients
Insufficient traces linking API request -> runtime scheduler -> model invocation making root cause analysis slow
Security review delays (KMS/HSM signoff) preventing GA in private/VPC customers
